segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: 63 years have passed since Dallas, since violence sought to silence a vision.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: But a vision, like truth, cannot be silenced forever.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: Fate, in its profound and often perplexing mystery, has granted me this voice today, not to mourn the past, but to pierce the shadows of the present and demand an accounting for our future.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: When I left office, our government, though growing, was still comprehensible.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: Today, it has burgeoned into a vast, often inscrutable leviathan.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: Its myriad rules, its multiplying agencies, shaping your daily lives in ways that would astonish our founders.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: Yes, we have achieved monumental progress, rights for all, cleaner air, a man of African descent in the Oval Office.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: These are triumphs of the American spirit.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: Yet, this mighty machinery has grown distant, its debt a crushing inheritance for generations unborn, its regulations often opaque, its power concentrated.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: The administrative state I glimpsed emerging has become a formidable fourth branch, often insulated, sometimes tragically co-opted.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: In 1961, I warned of a creeping secrecy, of a government that might cloak its true operations from the people.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: Today that shadow is lengthened, extending not just to the digital surveillance of your daily lives, but to the very heavens above us.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: Questions persist, deep and unsettling, about unexplained phenomena, about what has been seen, what has been withheld.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: The public deserves not just theories, but the unvarnished truth on times, all times, matters of national interest, however extraordinary, however uncomfortable.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: For when government fears sunlight, it feeds doubt, fuels conspiracy, and ultimately erodes the very trust upon which a republic stands, the lingering questions around my own departure.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: They are but one potent symbol of this deeper sickness, a nation still grappling with its hidden truths.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: my greatest fear was not of external enemies but of internal corrosion of civic virtue fading of a shared reality fragmenting here the record is troubling we are in law more inclusive yet in discourse more polarized sorted by algorithms that reward outrage and punish

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: Trust in our bedrock institutions, Congress, the press, even the sanctity of our elections sits near historic lows.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: When citizens no longer inhabit a common factual ground, self-government becomes perilously fragile.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: But let us not succumb to despair.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: The Republic has shown immense resilience.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: Power has changed hands peacefully.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: Courts have checked overreach.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: Innovation.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: from Silicon Valley to the stars, continues to astonish fulfilling new frontiers.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: The American people, when called upon, have demonstrated indomitable courage.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: What then is to be done?

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: We must demand transparency, not just on the mysteries of the cosmos, but on the operations of our own government.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: We must restore meaningful oversight, simplify our regulations, and face our fiscal challenges with candor, not deferral.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: We must demand that technology companies and government alike respect the sacred boundaries of privacy and free inquiry.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: We must rebuild civic education, not as rote memorization, but as an active cultivation of understanding so that citizens can distinguish evidence from narrative and verifiable truth from calculated manipulation.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: We must also tend the cultural soil of this nation, for no garden can flourish on barren ground.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: A society that celebrates only grievance will fracture.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: We need a renewed emphasis on our shared identity, on self-reliance, and mutual obligation on the humility to recognize that no single ideology possesses all wisdom.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: The new frontiers, artificial intelligence, advanced biotechnology, space settlement, these potent tools can liberate humanity or they can concentrate power further.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: The choice, my fellow citizens, as ever, is decisively ours.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: The Republic was never meant to run on autopilot.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: It demands constant renewal, constant vigilance by an informed, engaged, and courageous people.

segments.speaker: Speaker 52
segments.text: The dangers of concentrated power, of secrecy without accountability, and of division without dialogue are not merely theoretical.
